result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You had surgery on your right knee. You had a knee replacement (total knee arthroplasty) many years ago. Your knee had slowly become more sore and painful.

An X-ray showed the plastic part (poly) was very worn out. You had a poly exchange (revision) of your right knee replacement. The patellar and tibial plastic parts were replaced.

You recovered well. With physical therapy, you could walk with a little help. A nerve block (femoral nerve block) was removed by the anesthesia team. You did well on pain pills taken by mouth.

Your INR was 1.9 when you left. Your condition on discharge was stable.

## What you need to do
1. Go home. Your son will care for you.
2. Put weight on your right leg as much as you can manage (weight bear as tolerated).
3. Keep doing your physical therapy exercises.
4. Have lab checks twice a week.
5. Restart your home medicines. The letter does not say which ones.
6. See Dr. ABC in 2 weeks.

## Dates and medicines
- See Dr. ABC in 2 weeks.
- The letter gives no dates for your surgery or hospital stay.
- Coumadin: 4 mg a day. Your INR was 1.9 when you left. You need lab checks twice a week.
- Vicodin 5/500 mg: take 1 to 2 tablets by mouth every 4 to 6 hours.
- Home medicines: restart them. The letter does not list which ones.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- Which home medicines should I restart?
- What does my INR of 1.9 mean for me?
- Where do I go for my lab checks?

## When to get urgent help
Call the office or go back to the emergency room if you have:
- more redness
- swelling
- drainage
- fever
- any worry about the operation or the cut (incision) site

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
